title: Ingress safety margin scripted estimates (hosted API peak) - 2029 Q4
content:
Purpose:
Quick experimental runbook with scripted heuristics for regional safety margins and prewarm sizing for hosted API peaks. This is a working note: assumptions, micro-calcs, and recommended targets for Q4 2029 capacity planning.

Summary conclusions (top-line):
- Target live headroom: 30% over 95th-percentile sustained tokens/sec for US regions; 25% for EU; 40% for APAC (higher variance).
- Microburst buffer (15s windows): additional 10% headroom reserved in ingress pools (hot prewarm).
- Prewarm pool sizing per region = max( (95p_tokens/sec * burst_multiplier) - active_reserved_tokens/sec, minimal_pool_floor ). Use floor to avoid cold-start tail latency.

Assumptions and inputs (scripted defaults):
- Observed 95p sustained token rate (last 90d) by region: US-West 1.2M tps, US-East 1.45M tps, EU-West 0.6M tps, AP-Southeast 0.25M tps.
- Typical model mix: 60% LLM-7B (low token cost), 30% LLM-13B, 10% LLM-70B (high token cost).
- Per-GPU effective throughput (mixed model weights): A100-80GB ~ 85k tokens/sec, H100-80GB ~ 140k tokens/sec, L4 ~ 22k tokens/sec (quantized small models).

Example per-region estimate (script step output):
- US-East baseline 95p = 1,450,000 tps. Headroom target 30% => target capacity = 1,885,000 tps. Add microburst 10% => provisioning target = 2,073,500 tps.
- Map to GPUs (prefer H100 for core pooled capacity): 2,073,500 / 140,000 ≈ 15 H100-equivalent GPUs. Round to 18 for N+R safety and regional placement.

Prewarm sizing heuristic: 
- Burst multiplier = 1.15 for 95p->instant microburst; hot pool covers 90th percentile of 15s bursts.
- Minimal_pool_floor = 4 GPUs (to avoid tiny pools causing thrash).
- Cold-start budget: keep 10% of dedicated capacity as flavor-agnostic warm buffer for cross-model bootstrapping.

Routing and fallback notes:
- Route by policy: prefer region-local capacity; fall back to adjacent region within same continent (latency-aware).
- When regional utilization > 85%, automatic spillover triggers to Dedicated overflow pool (lower-priority).
- Fallback to small-model quantized variants for non-SLA routes to increase effective capacity.

Operational knobs and tradeoffs:
- Increase headroom pct => fewer incidents but higher cost. Simulate cost delta: +10% headroom ≈ +8–11% monthly GPU spend (depends on GPU mix).
- Smart KV caching reduces tokens/sec by up to 12% for repeat prefixes—prioritize for US regions with chat-heavy workloads.

Open questions / action items:
- Run 30-day microburst replay with new headroom targets (JIRA-ENG-1428).
- Validate H100 throughput assumptions against recent compiler/kernel changes (assign: Maya).
- Decide prewarm floor per-region by Nov 15.

Appendix (quick script pseudocode):
1) fetch 95p_tps(region, window=90d)
2) capacity_target = 95p_tps * (1 + headroom_pct(region)) * (1 + microburst_pct)
3) gpu_equiv = capacity_target / gpu_throughput_profile(preferred_gpu)
4) gpu_alloc = round_up_to_safety(gpu_equiv, safety=1.2) // N+R rounding

Notes to reviewers: this doc is intentionally conservative on APAC due to region-specific demand spikes during local business hours and partner integrations. Feedback welcome; will convert to spreadsheet with scenario toggles after CL on assumptions.
